proof_summary: Write the coefficient as \(3^n\prod_{j<n}(9j+2)(9j+4)(9j+7)/((n!)^2\prod_{j<n}(3j+1))\), and for each prime \(p\ne3\) sum divisibility counts over \(p^i\); a six-case residue analysis modulo \(9\), together with monotonicity of counts by least residue, shows the numerator’s three classes dominate the two factorial classes and the \(3j+1\) class. For \(p=3\), the explicit \(3^n\) factor covers the denominator because \(2v_3(n!)\le n\), so the denominator divides the numerator.
